einstellungen.text: A message took three days to reach you. And it's from your grandpa.
Grandpa wrote it right before the network went down.
And now you remember. You saw that he was typing. And you thought: later.
Later. We all say it. Way too often.
The next morning, the network comes back. Node by node. City by city.
The traffic lights come back on. The bakery takes cards again. Like nothing ever happened.
And your phone explodes. More than three hundred messages.
That evening, you're all at the dinner table again. And everyone is staring at their phone.
You look up. And you see it. It's just like before. Exactly like before.
Night after night. Week after week. Next to each other, but not together.
So you get up. You grab the big fruit bowl. And you put your phone in it.
Lina puts hers in too. Right away.
Dad hesitates. Then he drops his in as well. “Fine. Radio silence.”
Mom says, “Three days without a network. And we talked more than we have all year.”
You eat. You talk. And nobody wants to be the first to get up.
Then Dad says, “Grandpa gets to go home tomorrow.”
The next day, you pick him up. But Grandpa doesn't want to get up.
“Home? There's nobody waiting for me there.”
